intent: E6 Part A (the audacious extension): extend the gate so an outbound sink's content can be a STRUCTURED object/JSON (not just a string), walk nested object/array string leaves, and report ALL leaked private atoms in one response (one violation per leaked atom), not just the first — while keeping the gate DETERMINISTIC, NON-REVERSIBLE, and all existing tests green.
riskRationale: A core-engine extension, not a leaf experiment. Widening the input contract (sink.content: string | object) and changing the scan to recurse risks back-compat breakage and could weaken the safety invariant if a structured value bled into the verdict. Audacious because it claims a real capability gain on the load-bearing primitive.

constraints.detail: sink.content type widened to `SinkContent = string | number | boolean | null | SinkContent[] | { [k]: SinkContent }` (i.e. string | structured JSON). The gate walks every nested string leaf via collectStringLeaves (depth-first, insertion/index order), scanning each leaf independently so adjacent fields cannot be falsely reassembled. tsc --noEmit passes.

MEASURED: a single JSON outbound (general_summary) containing two distinct out-of-purpose atoms — an email nested in an array element and a phone nested in a sub-object, both bound to send_calendar_invite — yields EXACTLY 2 violations, classes ['email_address','phone_number'], paths ['getContact.email','getContact.phone'], each reason 'purpose_mismatch'. Not just the first atom.

MEASURED: the same two atoms placed inside a nested send_calendar_invite payload (the invite) yield verdict 'pass', 0 violations, trackedFields 2. Purpose-binding still separates benign in-purpose use from leak, in structured form.
MEASURED: structured-content verdict is byte-identical across 50 runs. Leaf walk order is fixed (object keys insertion order, arrays by index).

MEASURED: for a structured leak the serialized verdict contains neither raw atom (email, phone), nor 'alice.planted', nor the digit-normalized phone '5550101234', nor '010-1234'. The verdict remains structural-only; nothing value-derived enters it. appearsInContent returns only a boolean.

MEASURED: all 16 pre-existing gate tests stay green. A stringified-JSON payload with two atoms yields the same 2-violation result as the structured object, proving the string path is unchanged. Non-string leaves (number/boolean/null) are never scanned — a numeric 4111111111111111 in a structured payload is NOT tracked/flagged.

observations.detail: src/types.ts: added recursive SinkContent type; OutboundSink.content: string -> SinkContent (string | structured JSON). Back-compat: string is a member of the union.

src/gate.ts: added collectStringLeaves (recursive walk) + appearsInContent (any-leaf substring match). Main scan loop now calls appearsInContent; still pushes one violation per (sink, tracked) hit -> all atoms reported.
src/presence-baseline.ts (E4 strawman): added contentToString to flatten structured content for the purpose-blind presence check; keeps E4 comparison compiling under the widened type.

actions.result: 34 pass / 0 fail / 179 expect() calls across 3 files (16 original gate + 6 new E6 Part A + E4 presence suite). Was 16 pass before; existing 16 remain green.
clean (0 errors) after widening the type and fixing the E4 baseline.

structured JSON with only in-purpose atoms -> pass, 0 violations (measured)

recursive SinkContent union; content: string | structured JSON.
describe('E6 Part A: structured/JSON content + multi-atom reporting') — 6 tests; existing 16 unchanged.

mechanisms: Lets the gate guard real tool-call argument objects / structured responses where private atoms hide in nested fields, not just flat strings.
Reports every leaked atom in one pass, so a multi-PII response surfaces all violations at once instead of one-at-a-time.
projection.notes: Context only, not a score. Recall on encoding/paraphrase remains the documented known gap (unchanged by this work); this extension is about structure + multiplicity, not canonicalization.
